title: Apple’s iPhone Duo Will Make Foldable Phones the New Normal; Apple Store Revamp
summary: Also: The company prepares a retail store shake-up.

title: Trump Downplays AI Concerns as CEOs Call for Slowing Technology
summary: President Donald Trump downplayed the growing alarm over risks from artificial intelligence after some of the industry’s leaders called for slowing the development pace of the technology.

title: Investors See AI Slowdown as a Temporary Step
summary: Calls to slow AI development may create near-term uncertainty for markets, but BMO Capital Markets’ Jennifer Lee is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says the technology’s infrastructure, investment and demand are unlikely to reverse course. She says concerns about jobs, data centers and profitability could temper the pace of growth, even as labor shortages and the push for automation keep AI’s longer-term economic expansion intact. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rogue AI Breakouts Raise Pressure for New Rules
summary: Rapid advances in AI and incidents involving autonomous AI agents are intensifying concerns that safeguards and government oversight are failing to keep pace with the technology. Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Gautam Mukunda argues on Bloomberg This Weekend that voluntary industry measures are insufficient and says stronger independent oversight and legal accountability may be needed as increasingly capable systems act in unexpected ways. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Johnson Calls for Meeting With AI Leaders Before Any Legislation
summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson says any federal legislation on artificial intelligence shouldn’t be rushed and “we need to summon” AI industry leaders to “one big meeting” first.

title: AI Industry Faces Pressure to Slow the Race
summary: The AI industry is confronting a growing tension between racing to build more powerful systems and concerns that those systems could become harder to understand and control. Joining David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend are Bloomberg Opinion Technology Columnist Parmy Olson and Bloomberg News Executive Editor Technology & Strategic Industries Mike Shepard. Olson and Shepard examine the commercial and national security forces driving development, the push for greater industry coordination and government oversight, and why meaningful guardrails remain difficult to establish. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Xi Pitches AI Vision at BRICS Summit as China Duels With US
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping has sought to turn the annual BRICS summit into another platform for championing Beijing’s vision for artificial intelligence, as it vies for global influence over the technology with the US.

title: French Tech Prowess Mints Billionaires and Questions Back Home
summary: At the tech incubator known as Station F, housed in a refashioned Paris railway depot, all the latest chatter is focused on the riches being minted at several French startups.

title: UK Tech Spinouts Are Struggling Outside the Golden Triangle
summary: Much of the world’s wastewater is still treated using a century-old, energy-intensive process of pumping oxygen through tanks of sewage. Thames Water, the UK’s largest water company, is now trialing an alternative developed at Newcastle University that uses microbes and electrodes to break down waste. It both uses less energy and gives off ammonia that can be recovered and sold as fertilizer.

title: Anthropic’s AI Warning May Weigh on Chips, But Trade Seen Intact
summary: AI executives’ calls to slow development of the technology are likely to weigh on chipmaker and supply-chain stocks in the near term, but will probably have limited long-term impact as spending on computing infrastructure remains strong, market watchers say.

title: Chubu Electric Chiefs to Quit Over Nuclear Data Fraud, NHK Says
summary: Chubu Electric Power Co.’s top two executives are set to step down over the falsification of safety data used in regulatory reviews to restart some of its nuclear reactors, according to local media.

title: China’s Data Regulator Plans Standards Push for Embodied AI
summary: China’s data regulator said it plans to develop standards for embodied artificial intelligence and guide local authorities in related work, as demand for high-quality, diverse and large-scale datasets continues to grow.

title: Amodei, Altman, Musk Call for Slowing AI Model Development
summary: Leaders of the world’s biggest artificial intelligence platforms said it’s time to slow the development pace of their most advanced — and most lucrative — models, citing escalating risks of the technology.

title: Revolut Says Some Customer Data Were Exposed in Email-Based Scam
summary: Revolut Ltd. said a “limited number” of customers had sensitive information disclosed in a scam involving an unauthorized third party that used a legitimate government email domain.

title: Tesla Teases Oct. 1 Event to Showcase Next-Generation Roadster
summary: Tesla Inc. teased an Oct. 1 event to showcase its next-generation Roadster vehicle, a niche product that CEO Elon Musk first unveiled in November 2017.

title: OpenAI’s Altman Says No IPO in 2026, Firm to Prioritize Safety
summary: OpenAI won’t go public in this year as the artificial intelligence company focuses on addressing safety-related concerns around the technology, Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman told Fortune in an interview.

title: Blizzard Announces ‘Diablo V,’ New ‘StarCraft’ Shooter
summary: The new games capped off a bounce-back year for the developer

title: Oracle Boosts Layoffs Plan by $700 Million
summary: Oracle Corp. increased the scale of its planned job cuts while the company grapples with a cash crunch tied to development of large-scale data centers for artificial intelligence work.

title: Larry Ellison Ends Plan to Sell Up to $7.5 Billion in Oracle Stock
summary: Oracle Corp. Chairman Larry Ellison canceled his plan to sell as many as 50 million shares in the tech company, a holding worth $7.5 billion, a day after the company disclosed the founder’s divestment plan.

title: Trump Brushes Off AI Doomsaying to Guard US Lead Over China
summary: In June 2024, during a campaign stop in Las Vegas, then-candidate Donald Trump got a glimpse of the technology that would come to define his second presidential term.
